text: A bio fertilizer is different. It is a culture of living microbes that make nutrients available to the plant. Rhizobium in legume nodules, and Frankia in the roots of our own utis tree, fix nitrogen from the air. Azolla, a tiny water fern carrying the cyanobacterium Anabaena, is the classic bio fertilizer of rice fields. Azotobacter fixes nitrogen free in the soil. Some bacteria dissolve locked up phosphate. And mycorrhizal fungi extend the root system for phosphorus and water.
